Header. url: rights: public_reference why: Provides a highly quantitative, P&L-driven framework for unlocking working capital in e-commerce by optimizing specific financial metrics rather than simply increasing top-line ad spend. modules: [FIN] topics: [cash conversion cycle, liquidity risk, DTC e-commerce, financial modeling, CAC, AOV, maintained markup, sell-through rate, operating expenses, cash flow] tier: 2 scope_hint: comprehensive

Topics. cash conversion cycle (CCC) / defining the cycle as the time it takes to turn inventory into cash, acting as the primary bottleneck and measure of liquidity risk for bootstrapped growth; cost to acquire a customer (CAC) / lowering CAC to increase net revenue and speed up inventory turnover; average order value (AOV) / increasing AOV to drive higher gross profit without increasing fixed or marketing expenses; maintained markup (MMU) / increasing margins through supplier negotiation and retail pricing adjustments to dramatically reduce the amount of capital tied up in inventory; returning customer rate / boosting repeat purchases to drive net income, highlighting that 80-90% of profit comes from repeat buyers due to the absence of acquisition costs; 30-day sell-through rate / trimming underperforming SKUs and improving inventory management to unlock trapped capital and convert inventory back to cash; operating expenses (OpEx) / recognizing that cutting fixed expenses has a direct, 1:1 impact on net cash position, unlike variable marketing expenses.
The 1:1 OpEx Rule: The financial principle that fixed operating expenses have a direct 1:1 correlation with net income and net cash flow, whereas variable expenses do not.

The 60-Day Cash Lag: The observation that the exponential compounding effect of improving financial levers (like lowering CAC) is rarely visible in a 30-day window; it takes 60 to 180 days to reflect in the net cash position.

The Compounding Lever Strategy: The recommendation to adjust 2-3 operational levers simultaneously (e.g., cutting OpEx, raising MMU, and improving sell-through rate) to double a brand's net cash position without ever touching front-end marketing.
Zero-CAC Profitability: The concept that returning customers drive 80-90% of a brand's net profit because there is no marketing cost associated with reacquiring them.
Skip. The repetitive audio descriptions of reading out every single line item on the spreadsheet month-over-month, and the outro promoting the next video.
Scope mix. 20% baseline (basic accounting definitions), 80% growth (advanced financial modeling and liquidity optimization). Volume. ~350 words.
